newsitem.title: UK: UK's Wetherspoon pub chain bans alcopops.
newsitem.headline: UK's Wetherspoon pub chain bans alcopops.

text.p: British pub operator J.D. Wetherspoon Plc said on Monday it had banned the sale of 'alcopops' -- alcoholic lemonades and sodas -- from its pubs following the controversy about the drinks.

"Alcopops have had a lot of bad publicity and many people are concerned they may be attractive to people too young to drink legally. We simply do not want to be associated with the controversy," chairman Tim Martin said in a statement.
Alcopops are now the fastest growing sector in Britain's drinks industry, with annual sales of over 250 million pounds ($407.6 million).
But brewers have been accused by concerned consumer groups of targeting under-age drinkers with the drinks' bright packaging and youthful image.
The government last month announced measures to crack down on teenage alcohol consumption and is taking steps to regulate industry leaders.
A spokesman for J.D. Wetherspoon said alcopops would be banned from all its 194 pubs. Sales total around 10,000 bottles a week.
"They're not a massive part of our turnover," the spokesman said. Annual group sales exceed 100 million pounds.

He said the company, which has sought to distinguish itself by transforming derelict buildings such as banks and cinemas into pubs with large no-smoking areas and no music, was not launching a moral crusade or urging rivals to follow suit.
Wetherspoon said in April it planned to create 10,000 jobs across Britain and add more than 300 new pubs to its chain to grow beyond its London roots.
